steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
1. Clean, Connected Transit  
   • Expand electric-powered public transportation (buses, light rail, subways) and create safe walking- and cycling-first street designs.  
   • Integrate real-time data, unified ticketing and park-and-ride hubs so trips are fast and convenient, enticing residents out of private cars.  
   • Pair the mode shift with low-emission zones or congestion pricing to discourage high-carbon vehicles in dense cores.

2. Net-Zero Buildings and Districts  
   • Tighten building codes to require high energy efficiency, passive-design principles and electrified heating/cooling in new construction.  
   • Launch retrofit programs—incentives, green-bank financing, workforce training—to upgrade existing homes and commercial buildings with insulation, heat pumps, efficient lighting and smart controls.  
   • Procure 100 % renewable electricity for municipal operations and encourage on-site solar plus battery storage at the neighborhood scale.

3. Circular, Low-Carbon Urban Services  
   • Develop citywide composting and recycling infrastructures to cut landfill methane and keep materials in use.  
   • Promote local, plant-forward food systems via urban agriculture, farmers’ markets and sustainable procurement in schools and hospitals.  
   • Adopt circular economy policies (repair hubs, product-sharing platforms, deconstruction mandates) that reduce the energy and emissions embedded in goods consumed by city residents.
